topic: How do GEO versus LEO satellite orbits impact power flux density and resolution trade-offs in passive radar systems using Inmarsat and Iridium?
consensus_response: The choice between Geostationary Earth Orbit (GEO) and Low Earth Orbit (LEO) affects the performance of passive radar systems utilizing communication satellites as emitters of opportunity. Despite their different orbital heights, Inmarsat's GEO and Iridium's LEO orbits offer comparable power flux densities due to the trade-off between Effective Isotropic Radiated Power (EIRP) and distance. However, Inmarsat's larger footprint leads to increased interference, compromising system capacity, while Iridium's smaller footprint simplifies pointing but limits simultaneous illumination.
reference_context: Inmarsat's GEO and Iridium's LEO orbits have similar power flux densities due to the EIRP-distance trade-off. The wider bandwidth of Inmarsat is matched by larger antennas, while Iridium uses monopoles due to its lower data rate.
